source: Business Continuity Knowledge Base - Superior State

chunks.title: Company Locations and Network Ranges
chunks.content: Superior State operates from three location types. Office: 1101 11th Ave, Suite B2, Menominee, MI 49858. Home: two PCs connected via WireGuard site-to-site VPN. Cloud (IONOS): multiple VPS servers. Network ranges (Active): Office LAN is 10.0.0.0/24 with router at 10.0.0.1. WireGuard VPN network is 10.9.0.0/24. The office public static IP is 162.191.66.93.

chunks.title: Office Internet Edge - ISP, Modem, and Router
chunks.content: ISP: T-Mobile (office) (Active). Modem/Gateway: Inseego FX3100, management IP 192.168.1.1, reachable from office LAN 10.0.0.x, password-only authentication (no username). Router: Netgear R7000P (confirmed by dmesg), firmware DD-WRT v3.0-r62104 (os_version=62104). Router LAN IP: 10.0.0.1. Office public static IP: 162.191.66.93. Admin access: Web UI uses non-root username (reported: kevinmurphy), SSH uses root@10.0.0.1.

chunks.title: DD-WRT DNS and VoIP Observations
chunks.content: DNS forwarder: DD-WRT dnsmasq on 10.0.0.1. Upstream resolvers observed: 10.9.0.10 (WIN-DC01), 10.0.0.211 (DpathServer), 192.168.1.1 (Inseego FX3100). Phone.com lookups observed: sip.phone.com resolves to 72.1.46.10, polycom.prov.phone.com resolves to 72.1.46.93, _ntp._udp.clock.phone.com (SRV) returns NXDOMAIN and phone falls back to A record clock.phone.com. SIP ALG risk: nf_conntrack_helper observed set to 1 on DD-WRT router. Auto conntrack helpers / SIP ALG can cause SIP/RTP issues (failed registration, one-way audio). DD-WRT build had no tcpdump; visibility via /proc/net/nf_conntrack.

chunks.title: WireGuard VPN Architecture
chunks.content: Central VPN server: vpn-cube (IONOS), endpoint 216.225.207.204:51820, VPN subnet 10.9.0.0/24. DD-WRT tunnel peer (office site-to-site): Peer name 'VPN-CUBE', Allowed IPs via tunnel: 10.9.0.0/24 and 10.0.0.0/24, Persistent keepalive: 25 seconds, DD-WRT tunnel IP: 10.9.0.2/24. Design note: Office LAN devices do NOT run WireGuard clients individually. The DD-WRT router provides tunnel connectivity for the entire office LAN. Critical dependency: \\files resolves to 10.9.0.10 (WIN-DC01) and is VPN-dependent. If VPN is down, file shares are unreachable.

chunks.title: vpn-cube Server Details (IONOS Cloud)
chunks.content: vpn-cube (Active): OS Debian 12 (bookworm). VPN IP: 10.9.0.1. Public IP: 216.225.207.204/32 (ens7). Role: central WireGuard endpoint for office + home + VPS. NAT: masquerade out ens7 (supports VPN egress). Host firewall: UFW inactive; nftables INPUT policy accept with only explicit allow for UDP 51820. Inbound SSH exposure is Active unless restricted upstream by IONOS firewall (Unknown). DD-WRT router connects to this endpoint; office PCs do not run WireGuard locally.

chunks.title: Ubuntu Web Apps and Tomcat Configuration
chunks.content: Tomcat webapps under /var/lib/tomcat10/webapps: ROOT, beta, charlie, tst, old, commissions, nacha-combine (plus .war for each). Beta variants (beta, charlie, tst, old) are all test/enhancement variants of ROOT. Public URL reachability (all Active): superiorstate.biz/ (200), superiorstate.biz/beta/ (200), superiorstate.biz/charlie/ (200), superiorstate.biz/tst/ (200), superiorstate.biz/old/ (200), superiorstate.biz/commissions/ (302 redirect), superiorstate.biz/nacha-combine/ (302 redirect). Nginx routing: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled contains only superiorstate.conf. Port 80 redirects to HTTPS, port 443 terminates TLS and proxies to Tomcat at 127.0.0.1:8080.

chunks.title: Ubuntu Tomcat Service and Azure Integration
chunks.content: Tomcat runs as systemd tomcat10.service with JVM sizing -Xms512m -Xmx1024m. systemd drop-in points to EnvironmentFile: /etc/tomcat10/graph.env containing AZURE_TENANT_ID, AZURE_CLIENT_ID, and AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET (secret - do not store values). Azure/Graph usage: ROOT production is Not Used (Legacy), ROOT variants (beta/charlie/tst/old) are Active under test, commissions and nacha-combine do Not Use Azure. Redirect extra hop: /commissions and /nacha-combine redirect to http then nginx redirects back to HTTPS. HTTPS is enforced but with an extra hop.

chunks.title: Ubuntu Firewall (UFW) Rules
chunks.content: Firewall (UFW) on ubuntu (Active): Default deny inbound. Allow inbound from anywhere: 22/tcp (SSH), 80/tcp (HTTP), 443/tcp (HTTPS), 51820/udp (WireGuard). Allow inbound only from 10.9.0.0/24 (VPN): 3306/tcp (MySQL), 445/tcp and 139/tcp (SMB). Allow outbound: 25/465/587/2525 (mail-related). Which app/service uses outbound SMTP is Unknown. MySQL listens on 0.0.0.0:3306 but UFW restricts inbound 3306/tcp to VPN-only.

chunks.title: Scanning Workflow Overview - Scanner to eDrawer
chunks.content: The office scanning workflow moves scanned documents from the Kyocera scanner into eDrawer storage. Components: 1) Scanner device (Kyocera KM-2530 at 10.0.0.55) sends jobs to destinations. 2) Scanner File Utility on WIN-DC01 receives jobs and maps Save Numbers to folders. 3) Staging folders under \\files\Temp\Edrawer_Import receive scanned files. 4) EAR import app sweeps staging folders into eDrawer storage. 5) eDrawer storage is at C:\Shares\Company\eDrawer. Users access eDrawer via workstation installs + network share, no need to log into WIN-DC01.

chunks.title: Scanner File Utility on WIN-DC01
chunks.content: Scanner File Utility (Active): Runs on WIN-DC01 (10.9.0.10). Executable: C:\Program Files (x86)\Kyocera Mita\FileUtility\NsCatCom.exe. chunks.title: Ubuntu Backup Schedule and Retention
chunks.content: Ubuntu backups (Active): Scheduler: root cron '15 2 * * * /opt/backup/server_backup.sh' (runs daily at 2:15 AM). Remote: wasabi-linux: (rclone s3 remote). Paths: DB dumps at wasabi-backup-ssa/linux/databases/{daily|weekly|monthly}/<DBNAME>/, webapps tar at .../linux/webapps/{daily|weekly|monthly}/, server configs tar at .../linux/server-config/{daily|weekly|monthly}/. Retention: DB keeps newest N per tier (daily=3, weekly=2, monthly=3), webapps/configs keep newest 1 per tier. Legacy: older flat DB objects directly under .../linux/databases/{tier}/ (no per-db folder, reported deleted). Legacy script /usr/local/sbin/backup_beta_ssa.sh exists but not scheduled.

chunks.title: SERVER_22 Windows Server Backup
chunks.content: SERVER_22 Windows Server Backup (Active): Configured via wbadmin enable backup to target F: drive, runs daily at 20:00. Includes -allCritical (bare metal recovery volumes) and -systemState (system state). VSS option: COPY. wbadmin delete catalog was executed after schedule creation - this deletes local backup catalog metadata, NOT the backup data on disk. To rebuild catalog: wbadmin get versions -backupTarget:F: and wbadmin restore catalog -backupTarget:F:. 'wbadmin get status' returning 'No backup or recovery operation is currently running' is normal when nothing is active.

chunks.title: Paycom SFTP + PGP Secure Intake Pipeline - Overview

SFTP endpoint: superiorstate.biz:22. Vendor user: paycom. Vendor folder: /upload (server-side /sftp/paycom/upload). Encryption: vendor encrypts with SSA public key ssa_enrollment_pubkey.asc (uploads *.pgp / *.gpg). Decryption and handoff: automated on ubuntu every 15 minutes; decrypted outputs land in Windows-mapped P: handoff share (Samba [handoff] to /opt/phrd/handoff). Do not store private keys, passphrases, or SMTP credentials.

chunks.title: Paycom SFTP Server Configuration
chunks.content: SFTP host/domain: superiorstate.biz. Port: 22/tcp (reachable externally, vendor-tested). Host VM: ubuntu (IONOS), 10.9.0.12 (VPN), public 74.208.246.116. Vendor user: paycom (local Linux user). Group: sftp-only (enforces SFTP-only + chroot). OpenSSH sshd restrictions for group sftp-only: ChrootDirectory /sftp/%u, ForceCommand internal-sftp, X11Forwarding no, AllowTcpForwarding no. Chroot root: /sftp/paycom. Vendor drop folder: /sftp/paycom/upload (writable by vendor). Folder permissions: /sftp and /sftp/paycom are root:root (chroot-safe), /sftp/paycom/upload is writable by vendor with ACL granting svc-sftp-decrypt full access.

chunks.title: Paycom Decrypt Automation - systemd Timer and Script
chunks.content: Automated decrypt + notifications (Active): systemd service phrd-decrypt.service (Type=oneshot), runs as svc-sftp-decrypt, GNUPGHOME=/opt/phrd/.gnupg, executes /opt/phrd/phrd_decrypt.sh. systemd timer phrd-decrypt.timer runs every 15 minutes (OnCalendar=*:0/15), Persistent=true (catches up after downtime). Decrypt script behavior: selects newest unprocessed *.pgp/*.gpg in /sftp/paycom/upload, decrypts to /opt/phrd/handoff/<basename>.csv (unless basename ends with .csv or .xml), computes SHA256 for encrypted + output, logs rows/size, appends to /opt/phrd/state/processed.txt, moves encrypted original to /opt/phrd/archive/YYYYMMDD/, sends OK/ERROR email via /opt/phrd/send_mail.py.

chunks.title: Paycom Data Locations and File Extension Handling
chunks.content: Encrypted intake (Active): SFTP drop at /sftp/paycom/upload (vendor uploads *.pgp/*.gpg). Decrypt + processing artifacts under /opt/phrd: decrypted outputs (handoff) at /opt/phrd/handoff/PHRD_YYYYMMDD.csv (or .xml), encrypted archive at /opt/phrd/archive/YYYYMMDD/, work staging at /opt/phrd/work, state/dedupe ledger at /opt/phrd/state/processed.txt, logs at /opt/phrd/logs/decrypt_YYYYMMDD.log. Filename/extension nuance: script preserves .xml if encrypted filename is like something.xml.pgp (output becomes something.xml). If encrypted filename does NOT include .xml or .csv before final .pgp/.gpg, script defaults output to .csv even if content is XML. TODO: ensure Paycom includes real data extension before .pgp/.gpg.

chunks.title: Paycom Day-to-Day Workflow
chunks.content: Day-to-day Paycom workflow (Active): 1) Paycom exports enrollment data (LDExBEM 1.3 XML Structured) and PGP-encrypts using SSA public key. 2) Paycom uploads encrypted file to SFTP /upload. 3) Ubuntu automation decrypts and places output in the P: handoff location. 4) SSA confirms receipt + successful decrypt back to Paycom. Windows access: /opt/phrd/handoff is shared via Samba as [handoff] and mapped as P: on Windows. Samba share is read-only, uses force user = svc-sftp-decrypt, access restricted to Domain Admins and SUPERIORSTATE\kevinmurphy. Continuity note: SSA must retain matching PGP private key; if lost, historical encrypted files cannot be decrypted.

chunks.title: Operational Guardrails and Safety Rules
chunks.content: WinRM/double-hop rule: copies between two remote UNC paths (\\A to \\B) often fail with Access Denied. Prefer staged copies or interactive copy from one machine; document CredSSP explicitly if used. Long-running file copies: default to /NP and /LOG:, monitor via file size growth, Get-SmbOpenFile, or log tailing. Don't rely on scrolling console output. Hyper-V resource changes: CPU/RAM changes generally require VM Off unless hot-add is confirmed. Warn before attempting. Critical DC safety: ensure only one instance of DpathServer DC identity is online at a time.

GPG passphrase file: /opt/phrd/pgp.pass (treat as secret). SMTP notification env: /opt/phrd/keys/smtp.env (treat as secret). Key custody documentation is a High priority TODO.
